brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

A crowd supplies the upper stroke; architecture gives it structure; a cut-open mirror returns the world instead of a face. The flower crosses the outline like borrowed language. notes.note: Build a large, open-ended “I” from a crowd, an architectural shaft, and lunar ground: a speaking position assembled from material outside itself.
Open the tower at its center and introduce a hollow bronze mirror. The central image will be an aperture onto the supplied world, rather than an invented face.
Reveal Earth through the mirror’s removed center, reconnect only the tower’s foot, and let one botanical fragment cross the rigid letterform.

notes.note: The assembled letter is complete. Shift the mirror slightly left so its aperture holds an uninterrupted dark field around Earth, while retaining the off-center tower and crossing flower.

The final canvas holds a legible “I” without a human face: the crowd, interrupted tower, and lunar footing frame Earth in an open mirror. The single yellow flower breaks the geometry. No further changes are needed.
